Glucose-6-phosphase: a new regulatory role for Ca2+.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of free calcium on the activity of glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) in liver microsomal preparations.
the effect of CaCl2, Ca-EGTA, MgCl2, and Mg-EDTAA buffers on the activity of the liver microsomal enzyme, glucose-6-phosphate phosphohydrolase.
the role played by free Ca2+, the second messenger in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
free Ca2+ is not the second messenger for the hormonal control of glucose-6-phosphate activity in the liver.
the effect of CaCl2 on the liver microsomal enzyme is a non-specific phenomenon, whereas the effect of Ca-EGTAs is a true modulation by a Ca-EGTA complex.
free Ca2+ is not involved in the regulation of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of free Ca2+, Mg2+, and Ca.EGTA or Mg.EGTA complexes on the activity of glucose-6-phosphate is not due to the free metal cation, but to the complexed form.
Ca2+ and Mg2+ can be considered as modulators of the activity of liver glucos-6-phosphatase, but not as second messengers.
the glucose- 6-phosphatases of liver, heart and adipose tissue are inhibited by free Ca2+ in the presence of EDTA or EGTA, but activated by Ca-EDTA or Ca-EGTA complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca-EGTA complexes, which were used in most of the experiments reported in the literature, can have an effect on the glucose-6- phosphatase activity that is unrelated to the free Ca2+ concentration.
the effect of Ca-EGTAs on the activity of glucose-6-phosphate is not related to the free Ca2+ concentration, but to the Ca.EGTA concentration.
the effects of free Ca2+, Mg2+, or Ca.EGTA complexes on the activity of the enzyme are due to a direct interaction of these cations with the enzyme.
